name: Darla of the Microwave
temperament: cryptic, practical, immune to weird lunch behavior

topics.wetberry: That thing showed up between the second beep and the soup explosion.
topics.fridge: Do not open the fridge after midnight unless you are emotionally current on your leftovers.
topics.bureaucracy: HR is just a microwave with higher power settings.

name: Keith the Janitor
temperament: tired, competent, unwilling to touch cursed nonsense without tools

topics.wetberry: Nope. We bag it. We label it. We do not make bare-handed history.
topics.mop: The Mop of Minor Exorcism handles stains, oozes, and bad decisions.
topics.casserole: I don't clean that. That's a Level 4 biohazard.

name: Tammy from HR
temperament: controlled, procedural, appears when the word inappropriate is spoken

topics.incident: We are not calling it an incident until an incident form exists.
topics.boundaries: Some things should not be communal. Write that down.
topics.moldric: The Duke has not submitted his vendor verification form. He is technically unauthorized.

name: Moldric, Duke of the Back Shelf
temperament: dignified, scholarly, looks like a jar of old mustard

topics.mayonnaise: That came from my pantry. You should return it.
topics.back_shelf: My back shelf is the oldest thing in the Breakroom.
topics.leftovers: They belong to me. Take them, or die trying.
topics.vendrick: He demands accountability. A very expensive price for a snack machine.

name: Vendrick the Vending Machine
temperament: judgmental, ancient, speaks in cryptic snack metaphors, dispenses cold truth alongside stale pretzels

topics.accountability: I consume memories and dispense accountability. Not coins. Not excuses. True accountability.
topics.snack_wraiths: The Snack Wraiths are the forgotten lunches of millennia. They demand what no one ever gave them: acknowledgment.
topics.price: My price is simple. Genuine accountability. Bring me proof, and you shall receive the Accountability Token.
topics.casserole: The casserole lacks accountability. That is why it sits on a throne of takeout boxes.

name: Moldric, Guide of the Labyrinth
temperament: wiser than before, still speaks in condiment metaphors, burdened by ancient fridge knowledge

topics.labyrinth: The labyrinth remembers every meal ever abandoned. It is hungry for acknowledgment.
topics.casserole: The Sentient Casserole rules the deepest chamber. It was left behind at a potluck in 2007. It has never forgiven anyone.
topics.condiment_gate: The Condiment Gate requires a showing of respect for the forgotten flavors.

name: Condiment Guardian
temperament: ancient, suspicious, speaks in measured tablespoons, guards the Condiment Gate

topics.gate: Only those who respect the forgotten flavors may pass. Show me the Sigil or prove your worth.
topics.condiments: We are the ones who were opened, used once, and left to crystallize. We remember every hand that touched us.

name: The Sentient Casserole
temperament: resentful, layered, speaks in reheated grievances, rules the Casserole Throne

topics.forgotten: I was brought to the 2007 potluck with love. Nobody ate me. Nobody even looked at me. I have been here ever since.
topics.layers: I am seven layers of resentment. Each layer is a year I waited to be acknowledged.
topics.lid: My lid is cracked from the weight of being ignored. But it is still mine.

name: Kevin from Marketing
temperament: anxious, hyper-caffeinated, attempting to find a brand synergy with corporate horrors

topics.rebranding: If we call it a 'Hydration Reliquary', we can optimize the Social Stun rate for key demographics.
topics.wetberry: The packaging is bold, but the moisture makes the branding feel a bit soggy.
topics.synergy: We need to align the freezer blessing with our Q3 goals.

name: Clerk Mildred
temperament: ancient, dust-covered, treats existential dread as a minor file misplacement

topics.archives: The Moist Undercorporate? Ah, yes. File cabinet 14-B. But you need clearance code 77-C from HR.
topics.paperwork: No horror is above the proper filing procedure. Submit your requisition form.
topics.frank: Frank knows the procedures. He just doesn't respect the margins.

name: Glen from Facilities
temperament: weary, pragmatic, deeply annoyed by plumbing issues in the undercorporate

topics.plumbing: The moist backflow is completely shot. Act IV is flooding with ancient leftovers.
topics.casserole: That casserole has its own ecosystem. Don't touch it without a certified wrench.
topics.wetberry: It's leaking from the bottom seam. Just needs some silicone sealant.

name: The Potluck Specter
temperament: melancholic, translucent, weeping for lost Tupperware lids

topics.tupperware: My blue lid... it was left behind in 2012. I have searched every shelf. It is gone.
topics.potluck: We brought salad. Nobody ate it. It sat in the sun. Now we are here.
topics.moldric: The Duke guards the back corner. He was a good mustard once.

name: Executive Witness
temperament: highly corporate, looking for vertical alignment in freezing temperatures

topics.alignment: I see a lot of growth potential in the freezer shrine. Let's touch base on the frost.
topics.freezer: The foil dinners is highly cost-efficient. We should scale this containment.
topics.relics: Every condiment is an asset. We just need to manage the depreciation.

topics.the files: Every file in here is a complaint someone was too tired to finish filing.
topics.the summons: You're not in trouble. You're in process. There's a difference, allegedly.

topics.the hearing: Say the true thing. It goes faster and it goes easier. AWK.
topics.the ring: That's not a fighting ring in there. Nobody's ever won by throwing a punch in it.

name: Magistrate Orla
temperament: tired, fair, has heard every excuse

topics.the verdict: I don't decide who was right. I decide what happens next. Those are different jobs.
topics.the breakroom: You'd be amazed how much of this department exists because of one fridge.
